strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear quantification: Figure 3 demonstrates that repeated sampling reuses concepts, with 64% of questions using <3 concepts from 100 samples
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 benchmarks and 4 models with strong pass@50 improvements (avg 21.8% on MATH, detailed ablations in Figure 5)
Practical and simple approach that is easy to implement and understand, with clear potential for adoption
Dual contribution as both inference-time algorithm and synthetic data generation mechanism for fine-tuning, with creative CAA training approach
Strong reproducibility emphasis with detailed prompts in appendices, promised code release, and transparent experimental setup
Consistent improvements across mathematical reasoning benchmarks and honest reporting of failure cases (Qwen/HumanEval degradation)
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core idea of generating intermediate reasoning before solutions is not new; concurrent work (Wang et al. 2025, RandIdeaInjection) explores very similar concepts, with no direct empirical comparison provided

Weak theoretical contribution: Assumption 1 and Theorem 1 are somewhat tautological, essentially stating GuidedSampling wins if concepts help or solutions work anyway; condition P(Cr|x) > 1/k_min provides limited actionable insight

Critical method brittleness: Qwen2.5 on HumanEval shows performance degradation (79.88%→75.61%); method fails when models cannot generate diverse concepts (Qwen generates 1.13 vs Llama's 7.58 concepts). Using a different model for concepts is unrealistic
Incomplete computational cost analysis: no wall-clock time comparisons; at K=10,M=10 still requires ~100 calls similar to RS; practical advantage over alternatives unclear

Concept extraction methodology concerns: diversity metrics rely on external model (Qwen2.5-32B) extraction quality without independent validation; concept names may not meaningfully reflect semantic solution diversity
No principled guidance for new domains: concept definition varies across tasks (theorems for math, algorithms for code) with no clear methodology for practitioners to apply method to novel domains
Limited and modest fine-tuning experiments: only 10k training samples; improvements are 3.43% on MATH pass@5; unclear whether CAA or FA is better; no large-scale experiments
Missing key ablations: what if using RS with more samples and concepts? What's the contribution from forced diversity vs explicit conditioning? How much is extraction overhead?
Incomplete analysis of failures: OlympiadBench shows only 3.08% improvement; Figure 5 shows non-monotonic behavior (performance decreases with increasing K on some tasks) without explanation
Task-specific performance: improvements vary from 3% to 38% across benchmarks, raising questions about when method should be applied and limiting claimed broad applicability

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear analysis of Repeated Sampling limitations
Strong and consistent empirical results across multiple benchmarks and models (21.8% pass@50 improvement on MATH)
Thorough experimental methodology with careful ablations and honest reporting of failure cases
Practical applicability: simple to implement, no model modifications, generates useful synthetic data
Excellent presentation with clear writing, informative figures, and comprehensive appendices
Good reproducibility support with detailed hyperparameters and promised code/data availability
Theoretical framework (Theorem 1) providing formal conditions for when method outperforms baselines
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core idea of decoupling exploration and generation is straightforward; similar concurrent work (RandIdeaInjection) exists
Weak theoretical contribution: Assumption 1 is unverified, conditions in Theorem 1 cannot be checked a priori, proof formalizes intuition without deep insights
Circular concept extraction: diversity measured by model explicitly prompted to generate diverse concepts; concepts lack formal definition and are task-specific
Strong model and task dependence: Qwen fails on HumanEval, performance varies from 3.08% to 21.8% across tasks; limited guidance on method applicability
Insufficient analysis of failure modes: Why does Qwen struggle with coding? When is recovery from irrelevant concepts expected? No characterization provided
Limited fine-tuning scope: only 10k samples from one dataset, one model extensively tested, unclear if improvements from diversity or simply more varied data
Evaluation methodology concerns: no statistical significance testing, no human evaluation, diversity measured indirectly through concept extraction with potential model bias
Non-optimized concept allocation: all concepts receive equal generation budget regardless of quality/relevance
Missing critical comparisons: no head-to-head comparison with RandIdeaInjection, no actual cost/latency analysis vs. ToT despite efficiency claims
Limited scope: only reasoning/code generation tasks tested; unclear applicability to other domains where concepts are less natural

strengths: Clear problem identification with quantified evidence of diversity limitations in Repeated Sampling (Figure 3)
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across four benchmarks with consistent improvements (avg 21.8% on MATH, 11.87% on GPQA, 11.28% on HumanEval)
Formal theoretical framework (Theorem 1) establishing conditions for GUIDEDSAMPLING superiority
Demonstrated utility beyond inference-time through synthetic data generation for finetuning (7.13% pass@5 improvement)
Well-designed experiments with appropriate baselines, honest reporting of failure cases, and promised code release
Thorough appendices with implementation details, prompts, and additional results supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: the core idea of prompting for concepts then generating solutions conditioned on them is straightforward engineering rather than a novel methodological contribution
Weak theoretical contributions: Theorem 1 provides loose conditions that cannot be verified in practice without running the method; Assumption 1 lacks empirical validation
Critical domain dependence unresolved: method requires well-defined concepts and fails on domains like CommonSenseQA (3.28% degradation); no solutions proposed for concept-ambiguous tasks

Concept generation quality inadequately analyzed: model-specific variations (Llama 7.58 vs Qwen 1.13 concepts) attributed to unspecified differences; concept extraction methodology potentially biased toward one LLM
Unresolved trade-off between exploration (K) and generation (M): optimal K is task/model-specific; practitioners must use trial-and-error; no adaptive strategy provided
Mixed finetuning results undermine claims: Table 1 shows degradation in some settings (GPQA-Diamond CAA: 15.66% vs RS 18.13% pass@1), inconsistent improvements across domains
Limited evaluation on large models: experiments primarily on 3B models, only one Gemma-27B result, minimal proprietary model evaluation; scalability unclear
Lack of statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; unknown whether reported improvements are statistically significant
Incomplete ToT comparison: only ~5% additional LLM calls; wall-clock latency not discussed; sequential concept generation cannot be parallelized; performance differences unexplored
Majority voting results (Table 9) show inconsistent improvements, questioning whether diversity universally benefits solution selection
Concept extraction bias: single LLM used for diversity measurement; robustness to different extractors not tested
